Subject: Payment API timeouts + 502/504 spikes in apac1

Hi Neha,

We started seeing a wave of 502/504 responses for our checkout flow in apac1 around 07:50 UTC this morning. Users report both timeouts and retries — our gateway shows rapid backoff retries that keep failing. Latency jumped from ~120ms to >2s for a stretch, and error rate peaked at ~18% for the 07:50–08:30 window.

Attached is a short log excerpt (apac-lb-502-sample.txt) and a trimmed prod log file. Important: these failures are directly correlated with high traffic from Redwood's inference endpoint we call for fraud scoring. Can your team confirm if there were capacity changes, rolling deploys, or routing adjustments in APAC?

We need an ETA for mitigation — this is a live checkout failure for thousands of customers. Happy to jump on a call now.

Thanks,
Sophie Tan
Head of Payments Engineering, MaplePay
ops@maplepay.com

Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment API timeouts + 502/504 spikes in apac1 — triage request

On 2028-08-19 09:41 PDT — quick notes from infra checks:
- No deploys or config pushes in apac1 at that time.
- Edge LB reported queue saturation on host pool apac1-euclid-03 and started returning 502/504 when backend connection attempts hit timeouts.
- We saw the LB spill to apac1-standby which had higher latency and fewer healthy backend streams.
- We also saw a surge of keepalive connection resets from a single client subnet range corresponding to MaplePay's request pattern (high concurrency, short-lived connections).

Immediate mitigation done at 09:38 UTC: increased backend pool max-conns, added temporary 10s circuit-breaker on client-side retries, and warmed a standby pool. Error rate dropped to ~4% after changes but customer still sees degradation on slow paths.

I'll keep monitoring; next: Rishi to confirm if any kernel-level failures were observed in model-serving that might amplify retries.

—Jordan
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Payment API timeouts + 502/504 spikes in apac1 — triage request

Checked serving runtime and model pools:
- No OOMs, no kernel panics. However, we observed sustained queue depth increase for the fraud-scoring model behind MaplePay's route; average inference latency for that model rose from 95ms to 650ms for the spike window.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~22% due to a hot prefix pattern; that increased compute per-request by replicating prefix decoding work.
- Continuous batching backpressure was triggered and some worker threads entered long scheduling cycles causing slow connect/accept times observed at LB.

Recommendation: temporarily pin MaplePay to a dedicated-sized pool (reserved capacity) to isolate from noisy neighbors and enable a short-term caching guardrail (prefer local prefix cache TTL bump). Also throttle MaplePay client concurrency via a per-route concurrency cap (we implemented a soft cap already).

I'll prepare an infra action plan and a tight rollback if the dedicated pool causes capacity ripple.

-Rishi
Staff SRE, Serving Runtime

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-08-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Payment API timeouts + 502/504 spikes in apac1 — customer update and next steps

Hi Sophie — thanks for the quick report and the logs. Quick summary and next steps: 

What we found:
- Cause: LB queue saturation in apac1 combined with a customer hot-prefix pattern that reduced KV cache effectiveness for your fraud model, amplifying per-request CPU and latency.
- Impact window: 2028-08-19 07:50–08:30 UTC; peak error rate ~18%, mitigated to ~4% after emergency pool adjustments.

What we did:
- Increased backend pool capacity and warmed standby hosts (09:38 UTC).
- Applied a soft client-side retry circuit-breaker to limit retry amplification.
- Implemented a per-route concurrency soft cap for MaplePay and a temporary dedicated serving pool for their fraud model.

Next steps (action items and owners):
- Rishi: provision dedicated-size pool for MaplePay for 72 hours and enable local prefix TTL bump (in progress). Target: 2 hours.
- Jordan: continue LB host health monitoring and roll a permanent LB scaling tweak to avoid single-pool saturation. Target: 24 hours.
- Grace: coordinate with MaplePay on traffic shaping and review their retry/backoff policy; propose client-side mitigations. Target: 12 hours.
- Neha: schedule a postmortem summary and request a joint call with MaplePay for 2028-08-20 16:00 UTC to review mitigations and follow-ups.

Sophie — we will keep the dedicated pool live while we monitor and will follow up with detailed metrics and a postmortem doc (JIRA MAP-8421). If you want immediate rollback of the dedicated pool, say the word and we'll revert.

Thanks again and apologies for the impact — we know this touches revenue and user experience.

Regards,
